title: Retry with Backoff and Jitter
subtitle: Retries help until every client retries at the same moment
motto: Spread the retries, or the retries become the outage
keyInsight: Backoff spaces retries apart but only jitter stops clients that failed together from retrying together.

decisions.title: Full jitter, not equal or decorrelated jitter
decisions.description: Each wait is a random value between zero and the doubled wait. It spreads clients across the widest range and is the variant the AWS guidance recommends.
decisions.alternatives: Equal jitter guarantees a minimum wait, but it clusters retries in the upper half of the range and spreads load less.

decisions.title: Reject excess attempts instead of queueing them
decisions.description: The simulated server serves what fits in each 100 ms tick and answers 503 to the rest, which is how an overloaded server without a queue behaves and makes synchronized waves visible.
decisions.alternatives: A server with a deep queue absorbs the burst, which is realistic for some systems, but it hides the effect of retry timing that the chapter teaches.

decisions.title: Cap retries as the trade-off
decisions.description: The trade-off frame limits retries to 2, so learners see that fewer retries mean less extra load and more clients giving up.
decisions.alternatives: Simulating a retry budget across the whole client population is closer to production, but it needs shared state between clients that the simple model does not have.
